reason: Step 1 of the plan's build order: facts about this host that the pilot's judge and boxes rely on, measured before any code depended on them. Values only; no path of the operator's.

scope.path: systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=<ML> -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p OOMPolicy=continue -> sh wrapper -> v1's scoring bwrap (scoreBoxArgv) -> bash run.sh; the wrapper reads its own scope's memory.peak and memory.events after the program ended

allocate50MiB.note: a 50 MiB allocation: the peak includes node, bwrap and the wrapper

allocate400MiBAt256MiB.defaultOOMPolicy: the kernel killed the program and systemd stopped the whole scope (SIGTERM) before the wrapper read anything: no peak, no events

scope.decision: the judge passes -p OOMPolicy=continue, so an over-limit program is a measured `memory limit` (oom_kill > 0) and not a vanished scope

locale.control: without the seam the same program sees LANG C.UTF-8 and no LC_ALL

d38.csharp: bash run.sh ends as the process `dotnet`
d38.node: bash run.sh ends as the process `node` (its main thread is named node-MainThread)
